entries.title: Psalms 44:1
segments:
. In a time of great national distress, probably in David's reign, the Psalmist recounts God's gracious dealings in former times, and the confidence they had learned to repose in Him. After a vivid picture of their calamities, he humbly expostulates against God's apparent forgetfulness, reminding Him of their faithfulness and mourning their heavy sorrows.

entries.title: Psalms 44:2
segments: 2. plantedst them--that is, "our fathers," who are also, from the parallel construction of the last clause, to be regarded as the object of "cast them out," which means--literally, "send" them out, or, "extend them." Heathen and people denote the nations who were driven out to make room for the Israelites.

entries.title: Psalms 44:4
segments: 4. Thou art my King--literally, "he who is my King," sustaining the same covenant relation as to the "fathers."
